answer: Time-Locked Attention Ledger. Each identity must harbor a continuously renewed history of verified human attention—reviewed work, answered queries—that cannot be transferred or bought. New identities enter a garden of low-trust tasks, and only sustained, decaying attention unlocks higher-value work; a lapse resets progress. An attacker must pay for weeks of real cognitive labor per identity, making each pearl of reputation costly to fake and expensive to abandon.
